incident: Colonial Pipeline - DarkSide ransomware (intrusion 29 April, ransom note 7 May 2021)

sources.title: Joseph Blount, written testimony, U.S. Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, 8 June 2021
sources.what_it_gave: detection ('just before 5:00 AM EDT' on 7 May an employee 'identified the ransom note on a system in the IT network'); Operations Supervisor at Control Center issued stop-work order, shutdown began ~5:55, all 5,500 miles confirmed shut by 6:10 AM EDT to keep malware off the OT network; entry via 'legacy VPN profile that was not intended to be in use'; Mandiant retained; restart evening 12 May; 950 employees, 29 refineries, 260 delivery points, 13 states

sources.title: CISA/FBI Joint Advisory AA21-131A: DarkSide Ransomware: Best Practices for Preventing Business Disruption
sources.what_it_gave: DarkSide deployed against the pipeline company's IT network; no indication OT was directly affected; company proactively disconnected certain OT systems; DarkSide initial access via phishing / remotely accessible accounts and systems / VDI (T1566, T1190, T1133); Cobalt Strike C2, RDP persistence, T1486

sources.title: Dark Reading (9 Jun 2021): Colonial Pipeline CEO: Ransomware Attack Started via Pilfered 'Legacy' VPN Account
sources.what_it_gave: VPN account had only single-factor authentication; complex password; ransom note found on IT network at 5:00 a.m. ET 7 May; legacy VPN profile shut down; DOJ seized 63.7 BTC (~USD 2.3m) of the payment

sources.title: The Hacker News / Bloomberg (Mandiant, Charles Carmakal): Hackers Breached Colonial Pipeline Using Compromised VPN Password
sources.what_it_gave: VPN account unused but active, no MFA; password later found in a dark-web batch of leaked passwords; first foothold 29 April 2021; ~100 GB stolen; USD 4.4m ransom paid; operations halted nearly a week

sources.title: The Stack: How the Colonial Pipeline hack happened (Mandiant findings)
sources.what_it_gave: Mandiant saw no attacker activity before 29 April; no evidence of phishing against the account owner; Carmakal: attackers did not move from the IT network to the OT network; no CISO at the time

sources.title: BNN Bloomberg (9 May 2021): Colonial hackers stole data Thursday ahead of pipeline shutdown
sources.what_it_gave: about 100 GB exfiltrated from the network in roughly two hours on Thursday 6 May, then computers encrypted; double extortion; Mandiant assisting

sources.title: BankInfoSecurity: Colonial CEO at Senate Hearing Details Ransomware Attack
sources.what_it_gave: legacy VPN 'essentially invisible' to IT, no MFA; decision to pay 7 May, payment 8 May; seven finance systems back online 8 June; FBI contacted the morning of the attack

narrative_before: DarkSide affiliates logged into Colonial Pipeline's network on 29 April 2021 through a legacy VPN profile 'that was not intended to be in use', which had only single-factor authentication and whose complex password later turned up in a dark-web batch of leaked credentials (Blount testimony; Mandiant via Bloomberg). On Thursday 6 May they exfiltrated about 100 GB of data from the IT network in roughly two hours and then encrypted computers (Bloomberg). Just before 5:00 AM EDT on Friday 7 May an employee found the ransom note on a system in the IT network; the Control Center operations supervisor ordered a stop-work and by 6:10 AM all 5,500 miles of pipeline were shut down to keep the malware from reaching the OT network, which Mandiant later confirmed the attackers never entered (Blount; CISA AA21-131A; Carmakal). Colonial paid about USD 4.4 million (75 BTC) on 8 May, of which DOJ later seized 63.7 BTC, and restarted the pipeline on the evening of 12 May; fuel shortages hit 13 states and D.C. served from 29 Gulf Coast refineries, and seven finance systems were only restored on 8 June (Blount; Dark Reading).

services.name: Refined-products pipeline operations (5,500 miles, 29 refineries to 260 delivery points in 13 states + DC)
Finance / business systems (seven systems offline until 8 June 2021)
Corporate IT network (encrypted systems, exfiltrated data)

detection_moments.description: Just before 5:00 AM EDT, Friday 7 May 2021: an employee finds the DarkSide ransom note on a system in the IT network. IT systems are already encrypted and ~100 GB was exfiltrated the previous day; the OT network is clean but is disconnected and the pipeline halted by 6:10 AM. No earlier detection existed - Mandiant found the intrusion began 29 April via the legacy VPN.
detection_moments.evidence: 'just before 5:00 AM Eastern Daylight Time ... one of our employees identified the ransom note on a system in the IT network ... By 6:10 AM EDT, they confirmed that all 5,500 miles of pipelines had been shut down ... to help ensure the malware did not spread to the Operational Technology (OT) network' - Blount Senate testimony; 'DarkSide ransomware was deployed against the company's IT network ... no indication that OT networks were directly affected' - CISA AA21-131A; 'about 100 GB ... in roughly two hours on Thursday' - Bloomberg

attack_path: 29 Apr 2021: valid-account login to the legacy single-factor VPN profile with a password from a leaked-credential batch (T1133 External Remote Services, T1078 Valid Accounts) into the IT network

Movement across the IT network to business/finance systems; ~100 GB exfiltrated in ~2 hours on 6 May (T1041/T1567) then DarkSide encryption of IT systems (T1486). Intermediate hop technique not published; CISA attributes Cobalt Strike C2 and RDP persistence to DarkSide generally (T1071, T1021.001)
ambiguities: No public source names the individual IT hosts that were encrypted or that held the exfiltrated 100 GB; 'srv_it_x', 'pc_x' and three of the seven finance systems are generic placeholders (rule 1, 3-10 per group).

The specific lateral-movement tooling inside Colonial's network has not been published; the intra-IT hop is attested only as an outcome (encryption + exfiltration). Cobalt Strike/RDP are CISA's generic DarkSide TTPs, not Colonial-specific findings.
No domain controller, file server or domain-credential use is mentioned in any source, so 'dc'/'files' omitted and no pc->dc links.

Blount said an employee found the note on 'a system in the IT network'; Bloomberg attributed it to a control-room employee - modelled as a workstation 'pc_ransom_note'. Whether that host was itself encrypted is not stated; risk 9 assumed because the note is the ransomware's output.
web_vpn given risk 5 (initial access only); whether the VPN appliance itself was modified is not stated.

OT (dev_ot_control) was never compromised (Mandiant) and was disconnected by Colonial, so isolatable=true; the shutdown was a precaution, not a safety constraint. Pipeline service value 25 (core business) rather than 30 since no source says loss of the service was life-critical, despite fuel shortages.

Services' replicas: sources do not describe redundancy; replicas=1. Whether pipeline operations depended on the encrypted billing/finance systems is widely reported but not stated in the Senate testimony, so depends_on left empty.
Ransom figure given as USD 4.3m (BankInfoSecurity) vs 4.4m / 75 BTC (Bloomberg, DOJ); 75 BTC figure is from DOJ seizure reporting (63.7 BTC recovered).
